title: Pīca et fīlius
summary: A slow walk with my son, a real question (alone or with the kids?), and a magpie with a plan. Iulia and Marcus.

intro.en: [mischievously] Today, let's talk about a walk, a little boy… and a magpie.
intro.la: [mischievously] Hodiē loquāmur dē ambulātiōne, dē puerō… et dē pīcā.

lines.en: [curious] Marcus! Are you walking already?
lines.la: [curious] Marce! Iam ambulās?

lines.en: [cheerfully] Already. But not alone today.
lines.la: [cheerfully] Iam. Sed hodiē nōn sōlus.

lines.en: I'm walking with… [short pause] with my son.
lines.la: Cum… [short pause] cum fīliō meō ambulō.

lines.en: [delighted] Oh, with your son! How old is he now?
lines.la: [delighted] Ō, cum fīliō tuō! Quot annōs nunc nātus est?

lines.en: Three. So we walk slowly. [sighs] Very slowly.
lines.la: Trēs. Itaque lentē ambulāmus. [sighs] Lentissimē.

lines.en: Is he holding your hand?
lines.la: Tenetne manum tuam?

lines.en: [laughs] No way. He's pulling a little pram.
lines.la: [laughs] Minimē. Currum puerīlem trahit.

lines.en: [surprised] A pram? Is there a baby in it?
lines.la: [surprised] Currum puerīlem? Estne īnfāns in eō?

lines.en: No, it's empty. That's just how he plays.
lines.la: Minimē, vacuus est. Sīc enim lūdit.

lines.en: An empty pram. [thoughtful] Unusual… but I like it.
lines.la: Currus vacuus. [thoughtful] Īnsolēns est… sed mihi placet.

lines.en: [chuckles] Unusual! You sound like my teacher in the phone.
lines.la: [chuckles] Īnsolēns! Loqueris sīcut magistra mea in telephōnō.

lines.en: Your teacher? What's she like?
lines.la: Magistra tua? Quālis est?

lines.en: Very good, honestly. And kind.
lines.la: Optima quidem. Et benigna.

lines.en: But she speaks too fast. And she always says…
lines.la: Sed nimis celeriter loquitur. Et semper dīcit…

lines.en: [playfully, in a bossy voice] In one go! Without a break!
lines.la: [playfully, in a bossy voice] Ūnō impetū! Sine intermissiōne!

lines.en: [laughing] Ha! Say it again, Marcus… in one go!
lines.la: [laughing] Ha! Iterum dīc, Marce… ūnō impetū!

lines.en: [groans] Slower, please. Enough! Let's go on.
lines.la: [groans] Lentius, quaesō. Satis est! Pergāmus.

lines.en: Okay, okay. A real question now.
lines.la: Bene, bene. Nunc vēra quaestiō.

lines.en: What do you prefer: walking alone, or with your son?
lines.la: Quid māvīs: sōlus ambulāre, an cum fīliō?

lines.en: [thoughtful] Hmm. That's a hard question.
lines.la: [thoughtful] Hmm. Difficilis quaestiō est.

lines.en: When I walk alone, I walk fast, and I think about Latin.
lines.la: Cum sōlus ambulō, celeriter ambulō, et dē linguā Latīnā cōgitō.

lines.en: When I walk with my son, I walk slowly… and I think about nothing.
lines.la: Cum fīliō meō lentē ambulō… et dē nūllā rē cōgitō.

lines.en: [softly] Maybe that's a good thing, though.
lines.la: [softly] Fortasse tamen bonum est.

lines.en: [curious] Why do you think so?
lines.la: [curious] Cūr id putās?

lines.en: Because then your mind rests.
lines.la: Quia tum mēns tua quiēscit.

lines.en: In my opinion, a slow walk is a gift.
lines.la: Meā sententiā, ambulātiō lenta dōnum est.

lines.en: [gently] And he won't be three forever.
lines.la: [gently] Et nōn semper trēs annōs nātus erit.

lines.en: [short pause] You're right. That's true.
lines.la: [short pause] Vērē dīcis. Ita est.

lines.en: Still… I prefer walking alone. [laughs] In the morning, at least.
lines.la: Tamen… sōlus ambulāre mālō. [laughs] Māne quidem.

lines.en: And after the playground? What happened?
lines.la: Et post locum lūdōrum? Quid accidit?

lines.en: My son went home with my wife.
lines.la: Fīlius meus cum uxōre meā domum iit.

lines.en: And I walked up the big hill. Alone. Fast.
lines.la: Et ego magnum collem ascendī. Sōlus. Celeriter.

lines.en: And then… [hesitates] how do you say it… a bird. Black and white.
lines.la: Et tum… [hesitates] quōmodo dīcitur… avis. Nigra et alba.

lines.en: [gasps] A magpie!
lines.la: [gasps] Pīca!

lines.en: A magpie. It followed me.
lines.la: Pīca. Mē secūta est.

lines.en: [worried] Oh no. Really?
lines.la: [worried] Ēheu! Vērē?

lines.en: Really. It flew straight at my head.
lines.la: Vērē. Rēctā ad caput meum volāvit.

lines.en: Once. Twice. [panicked] Three times!
lines.la: Semel. Bis. [panicked] Ter!

lines.en: I shouted, I waved my arms, and I ran.
lines.la: Clāmāvī, bracchia mōvī, et cucurrī.

lines.en: [laughing] A big man, running away from a little bird!
lines.la: [laughing] Vir magnus fugit avem parvam!

lines.en: [indignant] Don't laugh! It's a real danger!
lines.la: [indignant] Nōlī rīdēre! Vērum perīculum est!

lines.en: [still laughing] Sorry, sorry.
lines.la: [still laughing] Ignōsce, ignōsce.

lines.en: [seriously] But you're right. In spring the magpies are angry.
lines.la: [seriously] Sed rēctē dīcis. Vēre pīcae īrātae sunt.

lines.en: Because they have chicks?
lines.la: Quoniam pullōs habent?

lines.en: Exactly. They're protecting their young.
lines.la: Ita prōrsus. Pullōs suōs dēfendunt.

lines.en: [mischievously] Do you remember the kangaroo?
lines.la: [mischievously] Meministīne macropodem?

lines.en: [sighs] Of course. A week ago a magpie attacked a kangaroo.
lines.la: [sighs] Certē. Ante hebdomadem pīca macropodem oppugnāvit.

lines.en: And you laughed.
lines.la: Et tū rīsistī.

lines.en: I laughed. [short pause] And today the magpie laughed.
lines.la: Rīsī. [short pause] Et hodiē pīca rīsit.

lines.en: [playfully] Almost right: today the magpie laughed at you.
lines.la: [playfully] Ferē rēctē: hodiē pīca tē rīsit.

lines.en: [dryly] Thank you, teacher.
lines.la: [dryly] Grātiās, magistra.

lines.en: So where are you now? Still on the hill?
lines.la: Ubi ergō nunc es? Adhūc in colle?

lines.en: At the top. The magpie has left me. Finally.
lines.la: In summō. Pīca mē relīquit. Tandem.

lines.en: [calmly] And now my mind is becoming calm.
lines.la: [calmly] Et nunc mēns mea tranquilla fit.

lines.en: So, one last question. Alone, or with your son?
lines.la: Ultima ergō quaestiō: sōlus, an cum fīliō?

lines.en: [laughs] Tomorrow? With my son. [short pause] And with a big hat.
lines.la: [laughs] Crās? Cum fīliō. [short pause] Et cum magnō petasō.

lines.en: [laughing] Goodbye, Marcus! Watch your head!
lines.la: [laughing] Valē, Marce! Cavē caput!

lines.en: [warmly] Goodbye, Iulia!
lines.la: [warmly] Valē, Iūlia!
